glp1-action.title: How semaglutide works in the body
steps: Semaglutide travels in the blood, stuck to a protein called albumin. This keeps it working for days.
In the pancreas, it switches on beta cells. They release more insulin, mainly when blood sugar is high.
It also lowers glucagon, a hormone that raises blood sugar. This also happens mainly when sugar is high.
After a meal, food may leave the stomach a bit more slowly. This small effect seems to fade.
In animals, it reaches brain areas that control hunger. In people, trials show less hunger and smaller meals.
glp1-action.summary: Semaglutide lowers blood sugar when it is high and helps people eat less. These effects were measured in people. The stomach effect is small and seems to fade with time. Which brain areas take part comes mainly from animal studies.
glp1-action.caption: Semaglutide lowers blood sugar when it is high, and people feel less hungry.

insulin-glp1-hypo.title: Semaglutide with insulin or a sulfonylurea: the risk of low blood sugar
steps: Semaglutide alone lowers high blood sugar. Near normal, it works less, so sugar rarely gets too low.
Insulin lowers sugar too. So do tablets called sulfonylureas. They still work when sugar is normal or low.
Used together, they can push blood sugar too low. This is called hypoglycaemia.
So your prescriber may lower your dose of insulin or these tablets, as the label suggests.
Low sugar signs: sweating, shaking, hunger, confusion. Take sugar now. Can't swallow? Call an ambulance.
insulin-glp1-hypo.summary: On its own, semaglutide rarely makes blood sugar too low. With insulin or a sulfonylurea tablet it can, so the prescriber may lower those doses. Know the signs and take sugar at once. If the person cannot swallow, call an ambulance.
insulin-glp1-hypo.caption: On its own, semaglutide rarely makes sugar too low. With insulin or these tablets, it can.
